source.title: Hallucination Neurons and Where to Find Them: An Investigation into the existence of Hallucination Neurons
source.authors: Huseyin Cavus; Sebin Sabu; J. Spear; J. Kawatra; Pavithra Rajendran

record.tranche_reason: The study runs its own diagnostics and interventions on sparse neuron-localization claims, finding predictive and causal effects but also correlated alternatives, limited stability, and partial sharing. It refines the broader localization claim, though it does not measure the specific quantities or behaviors in V1–V7.
record.gate_note: The study reports detection, intervention, stability, correlation, ranking, overlap, and transfer results for H-Neurons. It does not audit neuron poles for named jobs, test explanations on held-out activations, or build attribution graphs. Related-work numbers attributed to other papers are not recorded as rows. The independent diagnostic replicate for Gemma TriviaQA is reported in Table 3; the authors state it had 10 H-Neurons and AUROC 0.820, gap +0.404, but give no further replicate metrics beyond the table entries.
record.test_reason: This is a diagnostic replication of hallucination-associated 'H-Neurons' in Gemma 3 4B and MedGemma 4B. It tests whether L1 sparse-probe neuron selections are unique, stable and shared, not whether neurons have one interpretable job. It does not audit neuron poles, score explanations by simulation, study InceptionV1 or build attribution graphs. It does not cite either original source. Its finding that selected neurons sit in correlated clusters, which the authors read as consistent with superposition, concerns a related construct (localizing a behaviour to neurons) and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that detection and population-level causal effects of H-Neurons replicate, but the selected neurons are not uniquely localized. Selections sit in correlated clusters, are moderately unstable, disagree between L1 and L2 probes, and are only partly shared across datasets and models. They recommend routine diagnostics that separate detection from localization.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts the H-Neurons identification pipeline using response-level rather than token-level labels, then applies CETT features and L1 logistic regression to instruction-tuned Gemma-family models. Adds correlation, bootstrap, ranking, intervention-control, and overlap diagnostics.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes detection, stability, correlation, L1–L2 overlap, and neuron-set overlap. The authors also report different detection performance between the two tested model checkpoints.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma 3 4B, 19 of 22 L1-selected H-Neurons have |r|>0.7 with a non-selected feature. Bootstrap Jaccard is 0.45–0.69 and L1–L2 overlap is 0–25%. The authors read this as selections drawn from correlated clusters, consistent with superposition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons picked by sparse probes for a behaviour (hallucination) are not uniquely localized: many correlated neurons carry the same signal.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse H-Neuron probes detect hallucination (AUROC 0.61–0.97) and transfer positively across datasets. Suppressing the selected neurons lowers judge accuracy modestly (2.4 and 0.9 points).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small sets of feedforward neurons carry predictive and modestly causal hallucination-related signal in Gemma-family 4B models.

fits_no_version.finding: H-Neuron sets are only partly shared: 4, 1 and 0 shared across Gemma dataset pairs, none across all three, and 3 shared across models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse-probe neuron selections for one behaviour are largely dataset-specific, with a small recurring core.

record.problems: Only two models are evaluated, both in the Gemma 3 4B family. The paper says the causal effect sizes are smaller than in the original report and does not test capability preservation after intervention. It did not perform single-neuron ablations of the candidate units. The diagnostic thresholds are described as empirical guidelines. Causal validation is reported for only two model–dataset settings.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or of shares with one, two or no understood jobs.
No interpretable-neuron shares measured for any model; only two 4B Gemma checkpoints are used.
No vision models, cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization.
No comparison of architecture, regularization or tools as drivers of interpretability rates.
No attribution graphs and no measure of behaviour explained by native neurons versus a replacement model.
No neuron explanations from activating examples tested against where neurons fire.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T5' is wrong for this claim. The study tests H-Neuron localization (Gao et al.), not whether neurons are already clean or interpretable, so it is reclassified as T6. Its correlated-cluster result is tangentially relevant to debates about superposition versus clean neurons, but it measures probe-selection uniqueness, not neuron interpretability.

versions.untested_parts: Does not count neuron poles with one or two named jobs or not-yet-understood poles, and does not audit Qwen3-32B.
Does not measure shares of interpretable neuron poles across models or scale to trillion-parameter models.
Does not study InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not compare architecture, regularization, or tools as causes of interpretability rates, nor estimate rates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Does not build attribution graphs or evaluate behavioral reconstruction by a model's own neurons.
Does not test whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
